imported_name_resolution.supported_signature: MissionManagerWire* cdecl(MissionManagerWire* manager, const std::uint8_t* flag)
imported_name_resolution.reason: The body opens with PUSH EBX and PUSH ESI and reads the first stack word from ESP+0x0c, so both operands arrive on the stack. ECX is never read on entry and is explicitly reloaded with the manager before each virtual call at 0x00fec3cb and 0x00fec3fd. The body ends with a bare RET at 0x00fec42a and the only caller cleans eight bytes with ADD ESP,0x8 at 0x00feca6f.

imported_name_resolution.note: The mission-manager classification is carried from the wave brief and is not confirmed by the analysis database: Ghidra holds no symbol here and SDKtoGhidra/SporeGhidra_march2017.xml binds no address for any FUNCTION_DEF. The receiver-shaped calling pattern is real, but the measured convention is cdecl with the receiver as the first stack word, so the model uses a cdecl prototype with the receiver first and returns that word unchanged. The model does not claim ECX binding.

order: Load the first stack word into ESI and read its vtable.
Call manager vtable slot +0x20 with ECX set to the manager, then call vtable slot +0x18 on the returned object; this is the first write stream.
Overwrite the first stack word with the dword 1 at 0x00fec3d6, so the payload word and the receiver word share one location.

Call 0x0093aa70 with the stream in ECX, the payload address, count 1 and mode 0. Mode 0 byte-swaps each element before the stream byte call, so the first write is a single four-byte big-endian word holding 1.
Read the second stack word as one byte and reduce it to bit 0 with AND BL,0x1.
Call manager vtable slot +0x20 again and vtable slot +0x18 on the result; this is the second write stream, obtained fresh rather than reused.
Test the masked bit and store SETNZ CL into the low byte of the payload word at 0x00fec41a, so the payload becomes exactly 0 or 1.
Call 0x0093a9a0 with the stream in ECX, the payload address and size 1, writing that single low byte.
Return the manager word unchanged in EAX.
mechanics.write_order: The four-byte word write always precedes the single-byte write, and both address the same payload location. Reversing them would erase the flag bit, so the order is behaviourally load bearing and is asserted by the model test.
mechanics.flag_bit_propagation: Only bit 0 of the flag byte reaches the record. The upper seven bits are discarded by AND BL,0x1 before the TEST. The resulting value is encoded as 1 when the bit is set and 0 when it is clear, written into the low byte of a word whose remaining three bytes stay 0 from the first write.
mechanics.payload_state: The payload dword is 1 for the first write and 0 or 1 for the second, so the second write leaves a word of 0x00000001 or 0x00000000 in memory. The receiver word is the same storage, which is why the model keeps a local payload and documents the aliasing instead of writing through the argument slot.
mechanics.write_modes: The first write uses mode 0 of 0x0093aa70, which byte-swaps every element; count is 1, so exactly one four-byte store is issued. The second write uses the byte-oriented 0x0093a9a0 with size 1.
mechanics.reacquisition: Both write streams are produced by a fresh two-stage virtual chain. A test that returns a different stream per call confirms the target does not cache the first result.
mechanics.receiver_return: The function is a chainable record initializer: the returned value is bit-identical to the manager word, so the pattern is call-then-assign. The model returns the same pointer it received and the test asserts pointer identity.
mechanics.no_null_guard: Neither virtual call result is tested. A null from either getter would fault in the original exactly as the unguarded dereference in the model would, and no defensive branch exists to observe.
mechanics.domain_separation: This is a persistence record initializer. It shares no state, no port and no type with the achievement manager paths in the sibling records 00676710.json and 00676ed0.json; the only overlap is the generic Opaque word and the thiscall calling convention.
